bl_lim_sem: The modules used declared no limitations.
bl_lim_intro: The limitations below are those of the method, not of this device in particular. They are stated so that the absence of a datum in the collected material is not interpreted as the absence of the datum on the examined device.

ld_titulo_doc_sem_extracao: Forensic Examination Report — Examination without extraction
ld_preambulo_nota_base: The acquisition operator is the one recorded, under seal, on the day of collection. The examiner who signs is the one who issues this report.
ld_preambulo_nota_senha: Both opened the session with their own password on this workstation; the password does not prove identity, and the tool does not verify it beyond that.
ld_preambulo_nota_declarado: Both data are declared; the tool does not verify identity.
ld_sem_objetivo: The examiner did not state the purpose of the examination or any questions.
ld_metodo_intro: The acquisition followed the guidelines of ABNT NBR ISO/IEC 27037:2013 (identification, collection, acquisition and preservation of digital evidence). The hash of each file was computed at the close of the acquisition, and every command output was preserved as part of the material.
ld_conteudo_erro: The content of this acquisition could NOT be interpreted for this report ({erro}). Nothing is asserted here about what the material contains.
ld_conc_vazio: It was not possible to reproduce the outcome of this collection from what was sealed in the acquisition. This report asserts neither completeness nor incompleteness of the material: the record needed to do so is not available.
ld_conc_integral: {resumo} All modules used concluded without reservation, and the acquired material is preserved under the integrity seal described in section 7. The limitations of the method are listed in section 5 and delimit what this collection reaches.
ld_conc_cancelada: Execution was interrupted before going through all the planned modules, so the acquired material is PARTIAL in relation to what had been planned.
ld_conc_falharam: There was a module that obtained no data. The absence of the corresponding material results from this, and does NOT authorize concluding that the data does not exist on the device.
ld_conc_ressalva: There was a module concluded with reservation, that is, which obtained part of the material and declared what it did not reach. Section 6 identifies which.
ld_conc_final: The material actually acquired is preserved under the seal described in section 7, and the limitations of the method are listed in section 5.

mod_android_estado_inicial_desc: Records the device as it was received: screenshot, power and lock state, battery level, foreground app and user profiles. Run FIRST: any other collection may wake the screen or bring an app to the foreground, and the state recorded after that is no longer the state in which the device arrived.
mod_android_estado_inicial_lim_0: Records the state at the instant this module runs. Any collection performed before it may have woken the screen or brought an app to the foreground — which is why it heads the list.
mod_android_estado_inicial_lim_1: The screenshot shows what was visible. Content protected by the lock screen is not revealed by it.
mod_android_device_info_desc: Reads the system properties (getprop) and produces a report with manufacturer, model, serial, system version, security patch, encryption, bootloader and verified-boot state, plus kernel, storage and battery. The raw command output is preserved alongside the report.
mod_android_device_info_lim_0: The specifications are the ones the device's own system declares. On a device with a modified system, these values may not match the real hardware.
mod_android_device_info_lim_1: Encryption, bootloader and verified-boot state depend on properties that not every version or manufacturer exposes. A field the device does not declare is reported as NOT DETERMINED, never presumed.
mod_android_identificacao_desc: Collects the IMEI (by several routes, with check-digit validation) and the accounts registered on the device — Google, WhatsApp, Telegram and others —, plus telephony and SIM data. It is what links the physical device to a person. LIMITATION: on Android 10+ the system may refuse to read the IMEI through the shell; the attempt and its refusal are recorded as evidence.
mod_android_identificacao_lim_0: Reading the IMEI depends on an interface that varies between Android versions and between manufacturers, and may fail. The raw output of each attempt is preserved, including the ones that did not obtain the number.
mod_android_identificacao_lim_1: The accounts listed are the ones registered on the device. This links the device to the account; it does not demonstrate who operated it.
mod_android_backup_logico_desc: Extracts the DCIM, Download, Pictures, Movies, Music folders and the app data area in shared storage, via 'adb pull', plus system metadata (getprop) and the list of installed packages.
mod_android_backup_logico_lim_0: It reaches shared storage — media, downloads and system metadata. The apps' private area requires elevated privileges and is outside this module.
mod_android_backup_logico_lim_1: An e-mail attachment is here only if it was downloaded to shared storage, and it arrives with no provenance: nothing in the material indicates which message it came from, from whom or when. That linkage depends on the e-mail app's database, which is in the private area.
mod_android_backup_logico_lim_2: From Android 11 on, the system restricts reading '/sdcard/Android/data' even in shared storage. The refusal is counted and declared — it is not the same as the folder being empty.
mod_android_backup_logico_lim_3: It copies what is present. A file deleted by the user is not recovered here.
mod_android_artefatos_sistema_desc: Collects the app usage timeline (usagestats), known Wi-Fi networks, notifications, battery history, processes, configured accounts and permissions granted per package. It answers when the device was used and by which app. CAUTION: this is volatile data — run this module early in the examination, as restarting the device discards part of the content.
mod_android_artefatos_sistema_lim_0: The artifacts are volatile: restarting the device discards a relevant part of the content. What is obtained is what the system still retained at the moment of collection.
mod_android_artefatos_sistema_lim_1: The retention window is Android's own and varies with the version and the manufacturer. Absence of a record in a given period does not demonstrate that the device was not used in it.
mod_android_artefatos_sistema_lim_2: The list of configured accounts says which services the device knows — e-mail addresses, messengers, cloud. It brings no message or file from those services: it is an inventory of accounts, not of content.
mod_android_bugreport_desc: Generates the Android bugreport: power history with screen-on marks, per-app usage statistics, system events, connectivity, packages with install date and retained logcat. It is the densest artifact available without root, and the one that best supports a timeline of device use. CAUTION: it takes from one to several minutes and may occupy tens of MB.
mod_android_bugreport_lim_0: The content varies with the Android version and the manufacturer; not every device delivers the same sections.
mod_android_bugreport_lim_1: The included system log is circular: it covers only the period still retained on the device at the moment of collection.
mod_android_bugreport_lim_2: It gathers system operation data, not app content — the user's messages, photos and files are not here.
mod_android_contatos_chamadas_desc: Queries the native Android Content Providers (content://call_log/calls and content://com.android.contacts/data/phones). CAUTION: the ADB shell may not have READ_CALL_LOG permission unless the device has root; in that case the provider returns 'Permission Denial' (recorded in the generated files) and the module tries an 'adb backup' of the dialer app as a best-effort alternative on devices running below Android 12.
mod_android_contatos_chamadas_lim_0: Without elevated privileges, Android may deny reading the contacts and call providers. The refusal is recorded, but the data is not obtained.
mod_android_contatos_chamadas_lim_1: The alternative route via backup depends on the app allowing it and was removed from the system as of Android 12.
mod_android_contatos_chamadas_lim_2: Via the backup route, it is Android's own agent that decides what is included: completeness is NOT verifiable, and the contact's name does not accompany the call.
mod_android_contatos_chamadas_lim_3: It obtains what the device retained. A record deleted by the user is not recovered by this route; recovering residue depends on a physical image of the partition.
mod_android_contatos_chamadas_alt_0_o: When direct reading is denied and the backup route is attempted, the device shows a confirmation prompt that must be accepted on screen.
mod_android_contatos_chamadas_alt_0_j: It is the only alternative route to obtain the data without elevated privileges. Without the confirmation, the backup does not happen and nothing is acquired.
mod_android_sms_desc: Queries the native SMS Content Providers (content://sms, inbox, sent, draft) and MMS (content://mms: headers, parts, addresses and attachments). CAUTION: the ADB shell may not have READ_SMS permission unless the device has root; in that case the provider returns 'Permission Denial' (recorded in the generated files) and the module tries 'adb backup' as a best-effort alternative on devices running below Android 12.
mod_android_sms_lim_0: Since Android 4.4, only the default messaging app has guaranteed access to the SMS provider. On a device without elevated privileges, reading may be denied; the refusal is recorded, but the data is not obtained.
mod_android_sms_lim_1: The alternative route via backup depends on the app allowing it and was removed from the system as of Android 12.
mod_android_sms_lim_2: Via the backup route, it is Android's own agent that decides what is included: completeness is NOT verifiable, and MMS attachments are not delivered.
mod_android_sms_lim_3: An MMS attachment is saved as parte_<id>.bin, with no presumed extension: the type the device declares is in mms_partes.txt.
mod_android_sms_lim_4: A message deleted by the user is not recovered by this route. Recovering residue depends on a physical image of the partition.
mod_android_sms_alt_0_o: When direct reading is denied and the backup route is attempted, the device shows a confirmation prompt that must be accepted on screen.
mod_android_sms_alt_0_j: It is the only alternative route to obtain the data without elevated privileges. Without the confirmation, the backup does not happen and nothing is acquired.
mod_android_agente_nome: Contacts, Calls and SMS via agent app (any Android version)
mod_android_agente_desc: Installs the suite's agent app on the device, which reads contacts, calls, SMS and MMS with its own permission, collects the result and uninstalls itself. It is the route for Android 12 onward, where the system backup no longer exists. IT ALTERS THE DEVICE (installs and removes an app).
mod_android_agente_lim_0: It obtains what the system providers deliver to an app with read permission. A record deleted by the user is not recovered by this route.
mod_android_agente_lim_1: Android may refuse the command-line installation (manufacturer protection or app verification turned on) or ask for confirmation on the device screen.
mod_android_agente_lim_2: Proven on Motorola and Samsung devices (Android 9 to 13) and on the emulator. NOT verified on Xiaomi/Redmi/POCO (MIUI and HyperOS), which usually require the "Install via USB" option turned on and a Mi account connected: on those devices the installation may be refused.
mod_android_agente_lim_3: The binary content of MMS attachments is not copied: the type and the name of each part are recorded.
mod_android_agente_alt_0_o: An app (the suite's collection agent) is installed on the device, is granted the contacts, calls and SMS read permissions, is run once and is uninstalled at the end.
mod_android_agente_alt_0_j: Without elevated privileges, and without the system backup (removed in Android 12), it is the only route to read SMS and calls. The agent only reads, has no network permission, and the APK used remains in the acquisition with its SHA-256.
mod_android_whatsapp_nome: WhatsApp — Media and Backups (best effort, no root)
mod_android_whatsapp_desc: Extracts, with no need for root, the media folders and the local encrypted backups (.crypt12/.crypt14/.crypt15) of WhatsApp and WhatsApp Business accessible in external storage. LIMITATION: the active msgstore.db database and the encryption key are in /data/data/com.whatsapp and require root for access.
mod_android_whatsapp_lim_0: The active message database and the key that decrypts the backups are in the app's private area, accessible only with elevated privileges.
mod_android_whatsapp_lim_1: The backups are preserved as they are, encrypted. This module does not decrypt them; reading them requires the key, in a later examination.
mod_android_whatsapp_lim_2: Without elevated privileges, the route to the database in the clear is the module that temporarily replaces the app, which alters the device and is express-selection.
mod_android_whatsapp_lim_3: ABSENCE OF MESSAGES HERE IS NOT ABSENCE OF MESSAGES ON THE DEVICE.
mod_android_mensageiros_desc: Extracts media and files in external storage from Telegram, Signal, Instagram, Messenger, Facebook, Snapchat and Threema, for those that are installed. LIMITATION: each app's message database is in a private area (/data/data) and requires root — absence of messages in this module does NOT mean absence of messages on the device.
mod_android_mensageiros_lim_0: It obtains what each app writes OUTSIDE its private area: photos, videos, audio and documents exchanged in conversation. The message database is in a private area and requires elevated privileges.
mod_android_mensageiros_lim_1: ABSENCE OF MESSAGES HERE IS NOT ABSENCE OF MESSAGES ON THE DEVICE.
mod_android_mensageiros_lim_2: Only the apps covered by this module are queried. Another messenger installed on the device is not examined by it.
mod_android_whatsapp_downgrade_nome: WhatsApp — Messages via temporary app replacement (no root)
mod_android_whatsapp_downgrade_desc: Obtains the WhatsApp message database in the clear on a device without root: it temporarily replaces the app with an old version that accepts 'adb backup', takes the backup and reinstalls the original. IT ALTERS THE DEVICE. Requires the old APK in 'binario/whatsapp_legado.apk' and Android earlier than 12.
mod_android_whatsapp_downgrade_lim_0: It depends on 'adb backup', removed from the system as of Android 12, and on the device accepting the installation of the old version of the app — which varies between manufacturers and versions.
mod_android_whatsapp_downgrade_lim_1: It obtains what the app retained at the moment of the backup. A message deleted by the user is not recovered by this route.
mod_android_whatsapp_downgrade_lim_2: The backup brings the app's private area, not the media in shared storage, which is acquired by the WhatsApp media and backups module.
mod_android_whatsapp_downgrade_lim_3: It reaches only standard WhatsApp (com.whatsapp); WhatsApp Business is not handled.
mod_android_whatsapp_downgrade_alt_0_o: The WhatsApp app is uninstalled with its data preserved, replaced by an old version and, at the end, reinstalled in the original version.
mod_android_whatsapp_downgrade_alt_0_j: It is the only route to obtain the message database in the clear without elevated privileges. The app data is not erased; the original APKs are copied and verified on the workstation before any change, so it can be undone.
mod_android_whatsapp_downgrade_alt_1_o: Interaction with the device screen to authorize the 'adb backup'.
mod_android_whatsapp_downgrade_alt_1_j: Android requires manual confirmation on screen to complete the backup.
mod_android_filesystem_dump_desc: Recursively copies /data/data (the apps' SQLite databases) and /sdcard. Protected files will be blocked if ADB operates in ordinary mode (User Shell).
mod_android_filesystem_dump_lim_0: Without elevated privileges, the apps' private area is inaccessible: the apps' databases are NOT obtained by this module.
mod_android_filesystem_dump_lim_1: What is reached is shared storage. Absence of an app's data here is not absence of that data on the device.
mod_android_apks_desc: Copies the .apk file of each user-installed app and computes its SHA-256, allowing a tampered or malicious app to be identified and submitted to later analysis. System apps are not copied. CAUTION: it may take several minutes and occupy considerable space, depending on the number of installed apps.
mod_android_apks_lim_0: Only user-installed apps are copied; those that came in the device's factory image are left out.
mod_android_apks_lim_1: An already-uninstalled app leaves no APK to copy — its absence here does not mean it was never installed on the device.
mod_android_apks_lim_2: The module preserves the binary, it does not analyze it. Asserting that an app was tampered with requires a later comparison with the official version.
mod_android_extracao_fisica_desc: Bit-for-bit cloning of the 'userdata' partition via 'dd', transmitted over a binary channel and with SHA-256 computed during acquisition. Requires root privileges or vulnerable legacy hardware.
mod_android_extracao_fisica_lim_0: It requires elevated privileges on the device. Without them there is no reading of the partition, and the result is an explicit failure — never a partial image presented as complete.
mod_android_extracao_fisica_lim_1: The image is of the user data partition, not of the device's entire storage.
mod_android_extracao_fisica_lim_2: The image preserves what the partition contained at the moment of collection. Physical extraction is not a synonym for full recovery: data the file system has already overwritten is not recovered by it.
mod_ios_identificacao_nome: iPhone Identification (model, iOS, serial, IMEI, number)
mod_ios_identificacao_desc: Reads what iOS declares about itself: model, version, serial number, UDID, IMEI, phone number and ICCID. It writes nothing on the device.
mod_ios_identificacao_lim_0: The values are the ones iOS declares about itself, with no verification against the hardware.
mod_ios_identificacao_lim_1: Phone number and ICCID appear only with a SIM present, and iOS may omit them depending on the carrier and the version.
mod_ios_identificacao_alt_0_o: The iPhone registers the workstation as a trusted computer (pairing).
mod_ios_identificacao_alt_0_j: Without the pairing, authorized on the device screen, iOS reports nothing to a computer. No user data is altered.
mod_ios_backup_completo_nome: iPhone local backup (messages, contacts, WhatsApp, photos)
mod_ios_backup_completo_desc: Performs the iPhone local backup through the same protocol as iTunes, without changing the device configuration. It brings iMessage/SMS, contacts, photos and app data (WhatsApp included), interpreted later in the Content Report.
mod_ios_backup_completo_lim_0: It obtains what iOS includes in the local backup. Deleted messages and files are not recovered, and apps that exclude themselves from the backup do not appear.
mod_ios_backup_completo_lim_1: A backup WITHOUT encryption does not bring call history, saved passwords, browsing history, Wi-Fi settings and health data: it is iOS's decision. To obtain them the encrypted backup is needed (the temporary-password module).
mod_ios_backup_completo_lim_2: If the owner set a backup password, the backup comes out encrypted and can only be read with that password. It is not the unlock passcode and cannot be bypassed.
mod_ios_backup_completo_lim_3: Messages kept only in iCloud (Messages in iCloud with optimized storage) may not be on the device and therefore not in the backup.
mod_ios_backup_completo_alt_0_o: The iPhone registers the workstation as a trusted computer (pairing) and notes the date of the last local backup.
mod_ios_backup_completo_alt_0_j: Without the pairing, authorized on the device screen, iOS delivers no data to a computer. No user data is altered or erased.
mod_ios_backup_cifrado_nome: ENCRYPTED iPhone backup with temporary password (brings calls)
mod_ios_backup_cifrado_desc: Sets on the iPhone a backup password generated by the suite, performs the encrypted backup — which includes the call history — and removes the password at the end. IT ALTERS THE CONFIGURATION of the device during collection; the iPhone asks for the unlock passcode on screen.
mod_ios_backup_cifrado_lim_0: It only works on an iPhone with no backup password set by the owner. With the owner's password, use the ordinary backup and their password.
mod_ios_backup_cifrado_lim_1: The iPhone asks for the unlock passcode on screen to accept and to remove the backup password: without someone to type it, the module does not proceed.
mod_ios_backup_cifrado_lim_2: It obtains what iOS includes in the encrypted backup. Deleted messages and files are not recovered.
mod_ios_backup_cifrado_alt_0_o: A backup password, generated by the suite, is set on the iPhone during collection and removed at the end; the removal is verified.
mod_ios_backup_cifrado_alt_0_j: Without an encrypted backup iOS does not deliver the call history or other sensitive data. No user data is altered; the password is in the record so that decryption is repeatable.
mod_ios_backup_cifrado_alt_1_o: The iPhone registers the workstation as a trusted computer (pairing) and notes the date of the last local backup.
mod_ios_backup_cifrado_alt_1_j: A condition imposed by iOS to deliver any backup.
mod_computador_copia_logica_desc: Copies the user's key folders (Documents, Desktop, Downloads, Pictures) found on the selected drive, with a SHA-256 hash per file for the chain of custody. It requires no special privileges.
mod_computador_copia_logica_lim_0: It copies only the user folders recognized by name — Documents, Desktop, Downloads and Pictures — at the root of the drive and in each 'Users' profile. Nothing outside those folders is copied, and the user's material kept elsewhere on the disk is not reached.
mod_computador_copia_logica_lim_1: Application data ('AppData'), where messengers, browsers and temporary files live, is not part of this copy.
mod_computador_copia_logica_lim_2: A file that exists only in the cloud and was not downloaded to the disk is skipped, and counted as such: the content is not on the computer to be copied, and the tool does not fetch it from the remote service.
mod_computador_copia_logica_lim_3: A refusal to read a file or a folder is counted and declared. Whatever is missing from the copy for that reason is never reported as absence on the disk.
mod_computador_copia_logica_lim_4: The copy preserves the files existing in the file system. Deleted files and unallocated space require the volume image.
mod_computador_copia_logica_lim_5: Reading is done on the drive already mounted by Windows. The tool writes nothing to it, but it interposes no write blocker and can assert nothing about what the operating system may have written when mounting it.
mod_computador_indice_arquivos_desc: Scans the entire drive and generates an index (CSV) with path, size, dates and SHA-256 hash of each file, without copying any content. It may take quite a while on large drives.
mod_computador_indice_arquivos_lim_0: The index lists what the file system exposes through the mounted drive. Deleted files, unallocated space, alternate data streams (ADS) and the file table ($MFT) are not reached by this scan.
mod_computador_indice_arquivos_lim_1: Folders the system refuses are not enumerated. Each refusal is counted and declared in the result — a file missing from the index due to a refusal is never reported as a file nonexistent on the disk.
mod_computador_indice_arquivos_lim_2: HexisForensics' own installation folder and the extractions root are excluded on purpose, so that the code and the evidence of earlier cases are not indexed as content of the examined disk.
mod_computador_indice_arquivos_lim_3: The index records path, size, dates and hash. No content is copied: it does not replace the logical copy or the volume image.
mod_computador_indice_arquivos_lim_4: Reading is done on the drive already mounted by Windows. The tool writes nothing to it, but it interposes no write blocker and can assert nothing about what the operating system may have written when mounting it.
mod_computador_artefatos_windows_desc: Collects registry hives, Event Logs, Recycle Bin, browser history (Chrome/Edge/Brave/Firefox), e-mail stores (Outlook, Thunderbird, Windows Mail) and Prefetch from the selected drive. It assumes the drive contains a Windows installation.
mod_computador_artefatos_windows_lim_0: It collects a fixed set of known artifacts, not the entirety of the system's forensic material: what is not on this module's list is not sought, and its absence from the extracted material says nothing about the disk.
mod_computador_artefatos_windows_lim_1: From the browsers, the history file of each profile is copied. Cookies, saved credentials, cache and downloads are not reached by this module.
mod_computador_artefatos_windows_lim_2: Run without Administrator privileges, or over the in-use system disk, files locked by the operating system cannot be read. Every refusal is counted and declared in the result, and is never reported as absence.
mod_computador_artefatos_windows_lim_3: The files are copied as they are, without interpretation: examining the content of hives, logs and history databases depends on a dedicated tool.
mod_computador_artefatos_windows_lim_4: The mail stores (.pst, .ost, Thunderbird mailboxes) are preserved as they are, and are NOT opened by this tool. The list of messages and attachments they contain requires a dedicated reader, in a later examination — what is here is the store, not its related content.
mod_computador_artefatos_windows_lim_5: Mail stored only on the server, with no local copy, is not on the disk and is not reached by any copy. Absence of a local store does not mean absence of correspondence.
mod_computador_artefatos_windows_lim_6: Hives and history databases are copied together with the files that complete them — the registry transaction logs and the SQLite write-ahead log. Without them, whatever has not yet been consolidated into the main file would be lost with nothing indicating the gap.
mod_computador_artefatos_windows_lim_7: Reading is done on the drive already mounted by Windows. The tool writes nothing to it, but it interposes no write blocker and can assert nothing about what the operating system may have written when mounting it.
mod_computador_imagem_fisica_desc: Generates a bit-for-bit image (.img) of the selected volume, reading the raw device through the Windows API, with SHA-256 computed during acquisition and a size check at the end. Requires Administrator privileges.
mod_computador_imagem_fisica_lim_0: The image is of the volume corresponding to the selected letter, not of the whole physical disk: it does not contain the partition table, the other partitions, or the unallocated space outside the volume.
mod_computador_imagem_fisica_lim_1: Areas of the disk that the operating system does not expose through the drive letter are not reached by this reading.
mod_computador_imagem_fisica_lim_2: Reading is done on the drive already mounted by Windows. The tool opens the volume read-only and writes nothing to it, but it interposes no write blocker and can assert nothing about what the operating system may have written to the drive when mounting it, before this run.
mod_computador_imagem_fisica_lim_3: The image preserves what the volume contained at the moment of collection. A bit-for-bit copy is not a synonym for full recovery: data already overwritten by the file system is not recovered by it.
